The report also criticized the White House for assigning Harris immigration responsibilities without adequate preparation and suggested that the campaign focused too heavily on defeating Trump instead of promoting Harris's own vision. The report was released in its unedited format despite acknowledging its shortcomings and did not include specific recommendations for future elections.

recent_articles.title: Israel deports foreign Gaza-bound flotilla activists after global outcry | Israel | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Israel** has deported all foreign activists seized from a Gaza-bound flotilla after global condemnation of their treatment in custody.  The **UK**, **Italy**, and the **European Council** have summoned Israeli diplomats for a formal dressing down, with many condemning the far-right national security minister, **Itamar Ben-Gvir**, for posting a video depicting activists being humiliated.  Human rights groups have documented widespread abuse of Palestinians in Israeli prisons, prompting criticism from within Israel and even from US officials who typically support Israel's policies. Greece also called for the immediate release of its nationals detained on the flotilla.

recent_articles.title: Quote of the day by American astronomer Carl Sagan: “The cosmos is within us. We are made of star-stuff. We are a way for the cosmos to know itself.” | - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Carl Sagan**'s famous quote, "The cosmos is within us. We are made of star-stuff. We are a way for the cosmos to know itself," highlights the scientific reality that human beings are composed of elements forged in stars billions of years ago. This powerful statement transcends mere science, suggesting that humans are intrinsically connected to the universe and carry a piece of its history within them. Sagan's work aimed to make science accessible and relatable, emphasizing the wonder and curiosity inherent in exploring our place within the vast cosmos.  His words continue to resonate with readers today because they remind us that despite our smallness, we possess an extraordinary ability to question and understand the universe around us.

recent_articles.title: Chennithala seeks report on parole granted to Periye murder convicts - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following protests from the families of the victims in the Periye twin murder case, **Kerala Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala** has requested a report on the parole granted to five convicts. The parole order was issued during the final phase of the previous Left Democratic Front government's tenure and the jail authorities clarified that prisoners are generally not allowed to leave during elections.  The family members of the victims plan to meet the Chief Minister and the Home Minister to file a formal complaint against the mass parole granted to the convicts.

recent_articles.title: Protests at new US consulate after Trump envoy says time for US ‘to put its footprint back’ on Greenland | Greenland | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Greenlandic** politicians and protesters gathered in Nuuk to oppose the opening of a new US consulate, citing concerns about increased US presence and potential encroachment on Greenland's sovereignty. **Jeff Landry**, the US special envoy to Greenland, arrived uninvited and sparked outrage with comments suggesting Greenland needs US intervention for national security.  The protest highlights growing tensions between Greenland and the US over the future of Greenland's autonomy.

recent_articles.title: US sanctions elected Hezbollah MPs and Lebanese security officials | Hezbollah News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **United States** has imposed sanctions on nine individuals, including members of Lebanon's parliament and an Iranian diplomat, accusing them of aiding Hezbollah and undermining Lebanese sovereignty. The US Department of the Treasury stated these sanctions are intended to deter those who aid Hezbollah's financial networks and obstruct peace efforts in Lebanon.  Hezbollah responded by calling the sanctions a "badge of honor" and stating they would have no effect on its strategic choices. Meanwhile, ongoing Israeli air strikes continue to target southern Lebanon despite a ceasefire that was recently extended for 45 days. The US is also brokering peace talks between Israel and the Lebanese government, with negotiations scheduled for June 2nd and 3rd.

recent_articles.title: Mother arrested after boys abandoned by road in Portugal
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Two French boys**, aged under five, were found abandoned by the side of a road in Portugal and their **mother and stepfather** have been arrested. The children were discovered near Alcacer do Sal on Tuesday with backpacks containing food and water but no identification documents.  The boys' father reported them missing from their home in Colmar, France, on May 11th. **Police in Portugal and France** are investigating the case.

recent_articles.title: Hungary to limit PMs to eight years in office, warding off any Orbán comeback | Hungary | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Péter Magyar**, leader of the **Tisza** party, submitted a constitutional amendment to limit prime ministers to eight years in office. The draft amendment would bar **Viktor Orbán**, who has served five terms as prime minister since 1998, from returning to the role.  The amendment also aims to dissolve the controversial sovereignty protection office and reclaim control of foundations that were previously controlled by loyalists of the previous government. This move is part of a broader effort by the new government to dismantle the constitution unilaterally rewritten and amended by **Orbán**'s Fidesz party and restore democratic checks and balances. The amendment, expected to pass with the support of the **Tisza** party’s supermajority in parliament, will be discussed next week.

recent_articles.title: Massive car crash in New Jersey pushes BMW into river; Indian-origin driver arrested after fleeing scene on foot - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A **BMW** driven by 32-year-old Zorawar S Kohli of Englewood Cliffs crashed into the Hackensack River Bridge on Route 80, causing the vehicle to plunge into the water. The driver escaped and was later found hiding under a train and arrested.  The crash also injured the passenger in the **Land Rover**, who was taken to a hospital with minor injuries.  **State Police** investigated the incident, leading to Kohli's arrest on charges of obstruction, resisting arrest, assault by auto, and other motor vehicle offenses.

recent_articles.title: Top UN court rules workers’ right to strike ‘protected’ in key treaty | Workers' Rights News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **International Court of Justice (ICJ)** issued a non-binding advisory opinion stating that workers' right to strike is protected under the 1948 International Labour Organization’s (ILO) Freedom of Association treaty. The ICJ, in a 10-4 ruling, emphasized that this opinion does not determine the exact conditions for exercising this right but is expected to influence labor laws globally. **International Trade Union Confederation** representatives hailed the decision as a victory for workers' rights and expect it will impact countries that have not recognized employees' right to strike.

recent_articles.title: Seems PTI will now have to 'resort to agitation', says MNA after party leaders yet again denied meeting with Imran - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ahad Ali Shah**, a member of the **Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)**, stated that his party would resort to agitation after being denied another meeting with former prime minister **Imran Khan**.  The Islamabad High Court has granted **Khan** twice-weekly meetings at Adiala jail, but restrictions have prevented him from meeting visitors for several weeks. The PTI submitted a list of six leaders, including Shah, for a meeting on Thursday but was denied access.  A caravan led by **Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi** to meet **Khan** was stopped in Islamabad and resulted in a sit-in at Chungi No. 26.
